evidence_02.objective: The attacker utilized an overly permissive cloud IAM policy. Edit the policy on the memorandum to implement Least Privilege (NIST 800-53 / CIS Benchmark). Restrict Principal, Action, and Resource.
hints: A wildcard '*' for Principal allows the entire public Internet to assume this role. Set it to 'arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ForensicsOfficer'.

Resource '*' exposes every bucket across the entire cloud account. Lock it down to 'arn:aws:s3:::case-files-archive/*' or 'arn:aws:s3:::case-files-archive'.

evidence_04.title: Evidence 04: The Zero-Day Patch (Coding / Logic)
evidence_04.subtitle: RECOVERED SOURCE CODE // /opt/archive/scripts/healthcheck.py
evidence_04.objective: The adversary weaponized a command injection vulnerability inside the system healthcheck utility. Inspect the Python code, replace the unsafe shell call with a secure subprocess invocation, and seal the zero-day.
evidence_04.vulnerable_code:
import os

def run_system_diagnostic(target_host):
    # VULNERABLE: Direct string interpolation into shell
    # Adversary input: '127.0.0.1; cat /etc/shadow'
    command = f"ping -c 1 {target_host}"
    result = os.system(command)
    return result == 0

patch_options.title: Patch Option A: Parameterized Execution (shell=False) + IP Validation
patch_options.code:
import subprocess
import ipaddress

def run_system_diagnostic(target_host):
    # SECURE: Strict input validation + argument array with shell=False
    try:
        # Validate that target_host is a valid IPv4/IPv6 address
        ipaddress.ip_address(target_host.strip())
    except ValueError:
        return False
        
    # Argument array: target_host cannot break out into shell metacharacters
    proc = subprocess.run(
        ["ping", "-c", "1", target_host.strip()],
        shell=False,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=5
    )
    return proc.returncode == 0

patch_options.title: Patch Option B: Subprocess with shell=True
patch_options.code:
import subprocess

def run_system_diagnostic(target_host):
    # Ineffective fix: shell=True passes string directly to /bin/sh
    cmd = f"ping -c 1 {target_host}"
    proc = subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True)
    return proc.returncode == 0
patch_options.flaw: Vulnerable! subprocess.run with shell=True invokes /bin/sh, preserving the command injection vulnerability identically.

patch_options.title: Patch Option C: Shell Echo Piping
patch_options.code:
import os

def run_system_diagnostic(target_host):
    # Ineffective fix: still spawns shell interpreter
    command = f"echo '{target_host}' | xargs ping -c 1"
    return os.system(command) == 0
patch_options.flaw: Still vulnerable! An attacker supplying 127.0.0.1' $(whoami) ' escapes the single quotes and executes arbitrary commands.

hints: Examine Option A: It validates the IP with ipaddress.ip_address() and passes arguments as a list without invoking a shell.
Option B fails because shell=True still evaluates shell operators (; & |).
Option C fails because quote escaping can be broken with command substitution $(...).

evidence_04.title: Evidence 04: The Deserialization Zero-Day Patch (Coding / RCE)
evidence_04.subtitle: RECOVERED TRANSACTION HANDLER // /opt/vault/handlers/sync_batch.py
evidence_04.classification: TOP SECRET // REMOTE CODE EXECUTION EXPLOIT
evidence_04.objective: The adversary weaponized an unsafe Python pickle deserialization flaw inside sync_batch.py to gain root shell execution. Replace the unsafe pickle deserializer with safe JSON schema parsing, and seal the zero-day.
evidence_04.vulnerable_code:
import pickle
import base64

def process_batch_sync(raw_payload):
    # VULNERABLE: Unsafe deserialization allows arbitrary code execution via __reduce__
    # Adversary payload: base64 encoded pickle with os.system('curl ... | sh')
    decoded = base64.b64decode(raw_payload)
    data = pickle.loads(decoded)
    return data.get('transactions', [])

patch_options.title: Patch Option A: Regex Keyword Filtering with Pickle
patch_options.flaw: Vulnerable! Pickle opcodes can build arbitrary objects without using literal keyword strings.

patch_options.title: Patch Option B: Strict JSON Deserialization + Typed Validation
Patch Option C: Running Pickle in a Thread
patch_options.code:
import pickle
import threading

def process_batch_sync(raw_payload):
    # Ineffective: threading does not isolate process memory or system calls
    result = []
    t = threading.Thread(target=lambda: result.extend(pickle.loads(base64.b64decode(raw_payload)).get('transactions', [])))
    t.start()
    t.join(timeout=2)
    return result
patch_options.flaw: Vulnerable! A thread still has full access to the host Python process and operating system.

hints: Pickle should NEVER be used on untrusted input because binary opcodes can execute arbitrary code.
Notice Option B: It replaces pickle with json.loads() and validates that transactions is a list.
Select Option B (Strict JSON Deserialization).
